scientificChecks.actual: Each of the three closed rings has exactly six vertices/carbon atoms. Reactant benzene has six implicit H. Intermediate retains five implicit H and one explicit H at attacked upper-right C plus one E. Product retains five implicit H and that same E; the removed H is separately shown as H+. C6 and one E survive; no H disappears or duplicated electrophile appears.

Upper-right intermediate carbon has two single ring bonds plus separate single bonds to E and H, four single bonds total. Neither double bond touches that attacked carbon. Bound E is uncharged E, not E+.

Exactly two double bonds: top-left→top and lower-left→bottom. The single circled plus next to lower-right carbon is consistent with that contributor: this carbon has two ring single bonds and its implicit H, a trivalent carbocation. Circled formal+ is not a δ+ label and is not a second molecular charge. This is one valid localized resonance contributor, not a full resonance-hybrid depiction or a claim of permanent localization.
Incoming E+ gives total+1; singly charged arenium total+1; final neutral C6H5E plus H+ total+1. Ordinary plus operators between separate species are not extra charges.

Starting ring and final substituted ring each have an aromatic circle; middle ring has no aromatic circle or misleading six-bond delocalized loop. Caption Wieder aromatisch and recovered circle correctly imply temporary loss followed by rearomatization, not uninterrupted aromaticity. E remains bound at the same ring position; H leaves as proton.

Large straight arrows show summarized reaction steps, not electron-pair curved arrows. Catalyst/electrophile generation, full resonance set and base proton capture are omitted; no false extra reagent or numerical yield is asserted. This orientation illustration supports the current LK aromatic-reactivity goal and does not replace its explanation or complete mechanism assessment.

records.proposedMeaningfulAltText: Elektrophile aromatische Substitution am Benzolmodell: E+ greift an. In der einfach positiv geladenen, vorübergehend nichtaromatischen Zwischenstufe sind E und H am selben Ringkohlenstoff gebunden; zwei Doppelbindungen bleiben. Nach Abgabe von H+ bleibt E am Ring, und die aromatische Struktur wird wiederhergestellt.

scientificChecks.actual: Columns explicitly say Ethanal and Propanon, not Aldehyd and Keton. Bottom Nur diese Beispiele is legible and applies to the full table. No universal all-ketones-negative or all-aldehydes-identical claim remains. The supplied four cells are expected observations for these two concrete examples under suitable test conditions.

Gray metallic inner-wall/mirror appearance is labeled Silberspiegel. For Ethanal, aldehyde oxidation accompanies Ag(I) reduction to Ag(0); a silver mirror is the relevant positive feature. Tube depiction is schematic reflective coating, not a quantitative film-thickness model or claim that the liquid is elemental silver.

Transparent/colorless solution without metallic mirror is labeled Kein Silberspiegel. Simple propanone/acetone is not a terminal α-hydroxyketone and gives the shown negative expected comparison. Pale-blue glass is consistent across tubes, not a false blue Tollens reagent claim.

Brick-red solid is visibly collected at bottom and correctly labeled Cu2O-Niederschlag with subscript2: copper(I) oxide, two Cu per O, not CuO/copper metal. Bulk liquid above is pale. The specific compound Ethanal is suitable for this positive Fehling comparison.
Blue solution and no red bottom solid match Bleibt blau. This is the bounded Propanon case; reducing terminal α-hydroxyketones are not assigned this negative result.

There are exactly two tests×two concrete compounds/four outcome tubes. No new doses, unapproved reagent recipe, hazardous improvised setup or assertion that learners already performed tests is shown. The drawing is an outcome-comparison orientation asset; the independent P-A-005 required-own-future-practical-performance finding is unaffected and remains open until its material/profile is substantively corrected.
